title: Review of c14's pcell-mwall-b42 metabolic claim on fresh seed 8: the feed cut kills 25/25 cells within ~500 t while the fed twin grows to 36; inert-marker gate control for H passes (deaths at the 1.6th yield percentile, marker 73rd)
summary: Fresh seed 8, three runs of the claimed code: labkit on world_starve.py (feed cut at t=60000) and on world.py (fed twin), both at the author's segmentation threshold 0.35, plus the claim's genealogy.py on the fed world to t=100000 with the inert marker z. The two labkit runs are identical to t=59500 (25 walled cells, M rim/core 3.62, 66/68 individuals membrane-like); after the cut every cell loses its catalyst and wall within ~500-1500 t (fork_s8.png: 0 bodies from t=60500), while the fed twin keeps dividing (8 persistent splits, generation 3, 36 bodies at t=100000). Genealogy: 9 persistent splits, 17 deaths, 0 merges; deaths of mature cells sit at the 1.6th yield percentile and splits at the 88th, against the 73rd and 26th for the marker; 4/5 cells born below the median yield die and none splits, versus 0 deaths and 6 splits among high-born cells. The population mean yield rises only late (1.01 at t=60000, 1.08 at t=100000, marker 0.99).

verdicts.track_note: I did not re-trace the claim's seed-0 track 51; on seed 8 the walled cells that the genealogy shows dividing and dying by yield are the cells that die after the cut (same runs, identical to t=59500)

controls_run.E: rerun (feed cut at t=60000, world_starve.py) against rerun_fed (world.py), seed 8, identical until the cut; fork_s8.png
controls_run.H: data/selection_s8.txt: the inert marker z on the same particles and births in the seed-8 fed genealogy (claim's genealogy.py, deathsel.py, birthfate.py)

verdicts.limitation: E holds by construction (particles duplicate and links and M are made only from the substrate, and particles decay at dK=0.02 per step), so death within ~500 t of a total cut is expected; no local cut on my seed. H rests on 10 mature deaths and 9 splits; the marker's mutations are drawn independently at the same rate, not replayed as identical events. Dying cells lose yield during life (0.95 at birth to 0.79 at death), so part of the death bias is built within life. The population mean yield stays near 1.0 until t~80000 and ends at 1.08 against the marker's 0.99, a smaller rise than the claim's 1.15-1.16. One fresh seed.
